text_fidelity_a:
KLOUD City Black gel comfort and anti-slip soft bike hand bar grip The pro to con ratio is pretty good with this grip set...

Easy to install: Barely finished half of a 16oz Natural Lite before they were installed, tightened, and the ergonomic outcroppings were perfectly adjusted to the contours of my hands.

Nice and squishy/grippy: Not the hard grips that give you hand fatigue, these grips seem to stay in perfect cohesion with your hands as you peddle down your favorite trail, and mini-jump over tree-roots.

Feel like a man while installing: These grips require a metric Allen wrench to install, not a can of your mothers "Aqua Net" like the grips of old.

One possible con for some is that there seems to be a little bit of play once the grips have been tightened down. Now; Will they hold up fine when a fat man hangs a wheelie on his Electric Purple Scott Seattle? The answer is "Yes they will!".... I know because I have tested that EXACT scenario. On the other hand, some of those v-shaped guys that manscape and ride "real" MB trails, may find the play in these grips bothersome or even dangerous.

Bottom Line: Great for the casual rider with carpal-tunnel, but if you are a serious mountain biker, I would suggest peeling off an additional 10 bucks....
text_fidelity_b: KLOUD City Black gel comfort and anti-slip soft bike hand bar grip

text_fidelity_a: Golf Rangefinder 1200 Yards, Rumia Laser Golfing Range Finder with 6X Magnification, Laser Rangefinder with LCD Touch Screen, Rangefinder for Golfing or Hunting with Voice Feature and USB Charing My ex goes out with our two sons regularly on the golf course.  His own father did that with him and his brother.  A nice way to spend a day walking in a nice setting and spend time talking with our boys, catching up on their lives.  This rangefinder was a way for me to contribute since I don't play golf and really have no great interest in the sport.  But having given this to my ex for his next golf date, I heard back from him that it was amazing.  He has always been old school, like his father - eyeballing the hole and gauging his shot, but having used this cool little gadget for the first time, he was struck by all the features that gave him loads of information like the magnification so he can zoom in to check out those difficult parts on a hole that can cause you to problems, or the touch screen and he loved the voice that talked to him so he didn't have to check on a distance by taking the rangefinder away from his eye - he could just listen to it.  This little guy is lightweight, too, so carrying it along on the golf course is not a problem at all.  One of my sons plays golf regularly with a group of guys he works with and told me that he would be getting this rangefinder to take with him next time they play.  Now, I realize this could be used for a few different things, like hunting, but it really is an ideal and extremely useful tool for golfers.  Considering what golfers pay for their clubs and membership to golf courses and such, the price of this gadget is fairly reasonable considering what it does.
text_fidelity_b: Golf Rangefinder 1200 Yards, Rumia Laser Golfing Range Finder with 6X Magnification, Laser Rangefinder with LCD Touch Screen, Rangefinder for Golfing or Hunting with Voice Feature and USB Charing

--------------

THE BAD:
-----------

text_fidelity_a: Franklin Sports Portable Backyard Croquet Sets - Complete 4 + 6 Player Croquet Sets with Mallets, Croquet Balls + Wickets Included - Outdoor Family Lawn Game Sets with Carry Bag I love this croquet set.  It is obviously good quality and should last for years.  It reminds so very much of the croquet set my dad had back in the late 1960's and we would play the game in the back yard.  His was even fancier than this set in that it had a metal basket on wheels to store everything in.  This set comes with a cloth carrying case.  The balls are well painted as are the mallets and end sticks.  It's very professional looking.  The mallets heads screw onto the handles and are reinforced with metal.  However, you must whack the head in the tightening direction to get it really tight and solid or it will start to unscrew.  The wickets are o.k.  I'd love to have wooden wickets but these do nicely.  This isn't the same kind of set that you will see professional croquet players in England use, theirs are much more substantial (and very expensive), but this set is perfect for years of backyard croquet games.

text_fidelity_a: TR Foldable Camping Chair Hard Arms, Portable Lawn Chair for Adults,Outdoor Chairs Heavy Duty with Mesh Backrest Cup Holder,Support to 300LBS (Camo) I recently got another camp chair from this same company, which we really liked. That one has a side table attach and sets up/takes down in a different way - folding flat. But when I saw this TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm I decided to grab it because we like the first one so much. We liked the quality, the material, and how nice it feels when sitting. I actually thought this one was going to open/close the same, but missed the design in the product page photos. No worries though - while it opens like so many chairs on the market now, I usually don’t like the style as almost all of the ones I’ve tried hurt across the back of my legs. I’m a shorter guy and they tend to dig into the back of my legs. Not with this TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm - I was pleasantly surprised. When it first arrived I thought I’d blown it, but thrilled to find out I hadn’t - it actually feels great sitting on. Also unlike the other one from this same company, this one does not sit straight up, with a more reclined position. It won’t be as easy to sit at a table and eat, but for relaxing it’s going to be great. Very easy to open and close, the set up of the TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm is as quick as can be. And can set up either fully open, or partially (almost fully) collapsed, making it easy to close and move, or set around waiting to go back into the included bag. The materials are great - thick, the canvas material feels great to sit on. There is a leather (or more likely, leather-like) arm material that also feels nice. Overall, the feel and durability both seem on the spot. I think we’re going to get a lot of years and use out of both chairs. The other one we have has the side table - which is great, but we can set the two next to each other, share the side table, and this one has a pouch on each side - not lined for keeping things cool, but the same material as the chair. Keep your phone, flashlight, keys, or drink in there. The bag fits like the all do and as most do, you’re likely going to need two people to get it in. I was able to get it out on my own no issue, but to hold that bag - which is “tight,” you’re likely better off with an extra set of hands. In the end, we like this TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm as much as the first chair we got from TR, and are thrilled to have added this one. They’re going to be great for camping, the beach or park, and even out back on nice evenings.
text_fidelity_b: TR Foldable Camping Chair Hard Arms, Portable Lawn Chair for Adults,Outdoor Chairs Heavy Duty with Mesh Backrest Cup Holder,Support to 300LBS (Camo)

text_fidelity_a: Franklin Sports Pro Pickleball Paddle – USAP Approved Paddle with MaxGrit Technology – Elongated Handle for Maximum Control First off, I am not a Pickleball paddle expert. I had one break off at the top of the handle while playing a game.  I think this Franklin Sports Ben Johns is a very durable, light weight paddle.  The grip feels good and I feel I have more control of the ball using this paddle than when I use my other paddle which cost about half.  I think spending $100.00 on a pickleball paddle (the cost of this paddle as of this review) is a lot of money so I don't want to come off as saying this paddle is the best because I doubt it is.  It's gone through a few relatively rough games with hard hits and ground smacks and is still looking almost new.  The sandy-like sticky texture wears off after a while but I don't particularly want it anyway.  I'm a novice pickleball player so keep that in mind and please read the reviews of those much more skilled in the sport before deciding to buy this paddle.  My game is tennis and I thought spending $90 on a tennis racquet was a lot of money and I love my tennis racquet.  But, after seeing a pickleball paddle literally break in half would probably convince me to buy the better ones.

Lifetime 90029 Portable Tetherball System A little tedious to put together, and arrived with one the needle/inflator missing. Luckily my husband had them on hand, and I received a discount from Amazon for the missing pieces.

It has held up well. We put water in the base, not completely full, just enough to keep it stable. It does not 'roll' per say. There are no wheels on it. You simply lean it towards its side and roll the base that way. I was worried at first it would be too heavy to move, but that hasn't been the case. We keep it out of the way, and when the kids want to play with it, they (or one of us) will roll it to the designated spot, and then back again. No problems whatsoever doing that. Meaning, it doesn't keep them from wanting to play because it's not in it's spot all the time.

Has held up very well so far. Three boys and adults have put this to use. The base is sturdy. The pole wobbles a bit, but it doesn't detract from play. It's not as sturdy as one you see at a school that is cemented into the ground, but it's still stable.

It's fund to watch the kids play against the adults and all the 'rules' they come up with to win. It has been well worth the money!!

Franklin Sports Cornhole Game Sets - Portable Cornhole Boards + Bean Bags - (2) Cornhole Boards + (8) Bean Bags Included - Perfect Beach + Lawn Tailgate Bean Bag Toss Game Set I tend to call this game "bean bags" but I guess "Cornhole" is the official name. It's a great game for a lazy afternoon with family or friends, or to set up when you're grilling. You set the tables up opposing each other and then take turns trying to throw your bean bags into the hole at the top/center of the table. Each player gets four shots. We usually score it three points if you get one in the hole and one if you get a bag on the table, but I haven't read the instructions to see what the "official" rules are. I'm sure every state has a regional variation of this game, and this set is good enough to play with whatever rules you want.

First of all, the tables are quite large. They measure about 2 feet by 4 feet wide. The tables have legs at the end with the hole that fold out so that they can be set up at an angle. I liked the material of these tables. I've played on sets that had a lot of give that allowed you to aim for the base of the table so your bean bag will slide right up into the hole. These sets feel sort of "dead" and your bean bag doesn't travel much. This requires a more skillful toss and it makes it harder to hit the hole. I like that because the result is fewer ties.

The carrying case is a large black bag with a zipper top. The tables fit into the bag, but it's kind of a tight fit. I tend to put the tables into the bag and then put the bean bags through the hole so that they sit between the tables. I have a Subaru Forester and the carrying case fits in that easily enough, but if you have a smaller car you might struggle bringing this set along to the beach. Also, it's a little awkward to carry, although it's not overly heavy.

If you're looking for a great cornhole set, this one is as good as anything out there. It sets up quick, packs away fast, and the carrying case helps protect the set while in storage. I like that it's labeled as a "professional" set, and it forces you to use good, precise tosses in order to win. Great fun at a grill, family gathering, or at the beach. Also, tossing bean bags is nice because if there are kids around they aren't going to get banged in the head by an errant horseshoe or something.

If you're looking for a family activity to help get your kids off their cell phones for a few minutes, look no further.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Cornhole Game Sets - Portable Cornhole Boards + Bean Bags - (2) Cornhole Boards + (8) Bean Bags Included - Perfect Beach + Lawn Tailgate Bean Bag Toss Game Set

Backyard Champs Cornhole Carry Bag If you own a cornhole set, you are well aware of the need to transport the set from your garage to your backyard, basement to car, etc. You could just carry the boards and bean bags the way they are, but a better option is to store the set in a carrying bag. And a good choice for the task is the Backyard Champs 2 x 4 Cornhole Carry Bag.

I got hold of this bag at the same time that I obtained a cornhole set, also from Backyard Champs. The idea of a carrying bag made sense, so I added it to my order. The bag is black in color and seals shut with Velcro flaps. It measures two feet in width, four feet in length, and eight inches in thickness. Thus, it has enough space to hold the cornhole set I own, which is from the same company. However, it may not be the correct size for other sets, so make sure you measure first.

The carrying handles on this bag are a little thinner than expected. They are also looped more widely than I feel they should be. A little less width, more like a briefcase handle, would seem better. The cornhole set I have isn’t too heavy so I think the handles will hold up, but there is still a little more looseness than I prefer. I hope I am proven wrong and that the manufacturer knew what they were doing when they designed the bag, but it just seems a little too loose for me. I suppose they made the loop larger so that you can place the handle over your shoulder but I prefer to carry it more like a suitcase.

Cornhole sets are often bulky and they need to be protected when transporting from one place to another. A carrying bag makes sense and the Backyard Champs 2 x 4 Cornhole Carry Bag is a good choice for the task. A little more snug fit and a separate compartment for the bean bags would make this bag better, but it is a good enough bag for the job.
text_fidelity_b: Backyard Champs Cornhole Carry Bag

text_fidelity_a:
FILA Accessories Home Gym Kit This gym arrives in a small box. It comes in 26 pieces with one tightening key and one written "exercise" sheet but no assembly instructions. I also needed to use a hammer (not included) when assembling the pull-up bar.

I am somewhat mechanically inclined, so I was able to use the visual pictures on the box (see last two pictures) to assemble the gym. The screws that attached the arms to the long bar of the pull-up bar caused me a lot of trouble. I eventually had to hammer the screws into the "square" hole when no amount of turning would screw them in. If it were not for that difficulty, I would have had this assembled in about 20 minutes instead of 45 minutes.

- The ab wheel is easy to use and rolls nicely on a carpeted floor.

- The push-up bars are a bit disappointing because the foam handles keep sliding back and forth when I try to do push-ups. The foam needs to be snug and not loose like it is. It requires certain positioning to keep these foam handles from moving.

- The pull-up bar is not something I will use as intended for two reasons. I feel like I will rip my molding off the door frame if I use this or mar my wall surface. Also, I am not (nor was I ever) strong enough to pull up my body weight. Nevertheless, this can be used on the floor as sort of a push-off bar as shown in the last picture.

Overall, I am disappointed in this set. The exercise sheet provided is not an exercise sheet at all. There are no assembly instructions, which is a requirement to me. I also do not like that the foam handles on the push up bars slide around and are unstable. If the foam handles stayed in place, I would have rated this four stars. However, because I consider that a defect coupled with the fact that not everyone will find it so easy to assemble without instructions, I am giving this three stars. Nevertheless, this is a low-budget option for those that do not mind the lack of instructions.

PHOTOS:
Photo one and two are the front and back of the only instructions provided, which is supposed to be an exercise sheet but has nothing to do with exercises. This sheet is a useless piece of paper to me. Photo three includes a picture of the two push up bars and the one ab wheel. Picture four includes the reverse (non-business) side of the pull-up bar and picture five is the business-side (the side where the user positions him or herself) of the bar. The last two pictures are the front and back of the box cover showing the product in use and is what helped me assemble this gym.
text_fidelity_b: FILA Accessories Home Gym Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Dreampark Portable Collapsible Outdoor Wash Camping Folding Basin Bucket for Camping Hiking Travel (8.5L, Blue) Before working with this water bag I was unfamiliar with the concept of using a nylon bag as a way to hold water, and I struggled a bit to determine how to use this bag. As it turns out, I found a very good use for it that is similar to holding water but is a variation on a theme. In short, this makes a fantastic ice bag.

I was a little surprised when this bag arrived as it is a little smaller than I expected. When unfolded and filled or just stood up it is a little bigger than a basketball. I had an image in my head that it would be bigger, like the size of a book bag or similar. This is not a very large bag but it does hold more than a gallon of water at a time, if you are so inclined to fill it with that much water and try to carry it.

The whole bag is made of nylon though there are three different types used. The outer shell is a parachute nylon which makes it very strong and also water resistant. The inner lining is a microweave type that holds liquid very well and is also very lightweight. The handle is a heavier type of nylon and is strong enough to hold the bag when it is full.

The product description says this bag will hold water so it can be transported from a source to a campsite or similar scenario. I found another good use. It is not a huge bag but it is larg enough to hold several soft drink cans and ice. So, filling this bag with ice and then putting in drink cans, you can keep a small number of cans cold and not drip water all over when the ice melts. This is a good option for when you are cooking out or you are having a small gathering and need to keep a few drinks cold without digging up a cooler.

This is an exceptionally lightweight bag and it compacts down very small. It is small enough to fit in a large pocket when it is completely folded up and packed in the little bag in which it comes. I have not put the bag on a scale but it definitely weighs less than a pound.

This is an interesting little bag. It is definitely waterproof and while it is marketed as a bag for carrying water it does serve some other uses too. It is small, lightweight and well-made.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: Dreampark Portable Collapsible Outdoor Wash Camping Folding Basin Bucket for Camping Hiking Travel (8.5L, Blue)

The scanner recognizes my index finger print only 20% or less. The fail rate is unacceptable! I tried resetting/ erasing my finger prints and trying again to have the safe save my prints. I made sure the scanner was clean and my fingers were clean before re-doing the finger print save process. Also, I made sure each print saved was at a slightly different angle/ position to increase chances of the biometric scanner reading my prints correctly. Unfortunately, the fail rate was still very high at over 60% fail rate. It was able to recognize two fingers almost consistently, but not to the point where I would trust it to be my main point of access option in an emergency situation. I would rather use the keypad PIN or keys for emergency accesss. I'm considering the VT20 that doesn't include the biometric scanner or trying another VT20i an see if this first one is just defective or not. The other minor issue is that the interior lining inside the safe is not flush on all sides and sticks out a little at the top of mine where the hinge is located. The last minor issue is the battery removal method using a thin string that you pull on to remove the battery. If this string were to break or the user accidentally forgets to push the battery into the battery compartment with string first then it'll be difficult to remove the battery for replacement. The user manual doesn't state anything about the string at all. It seems like a cheap and ineffective battery removal process that can lead to issues in the future. Without the string in place behind the battery it is difficult to remove the battery because it sits flush into the battery compartment with little room to try to remove it with your fingers. This unit does use a rechargeable battery, but eventually it does require a battery replacement once the battery fails or the user wants to get a higher capacity rechargeable battery.
The overall construction of the safe seems sturdy and well built. During my testing I stored a Sig P226 handgun with a Streamlight TLR-4 attached and four 10 round magazines inside the safe (one mag was in the gun). The fitment was tight, but I was able to close the safe. The Andriod app for the Vaultek safe worked well, but I wish there was an option to secure the app with a PIN code instead of only a pattern lock. The app is straightforward and easy to use. The ability to view a history log of how the safe was accessed, whose finger print was used for access if biometric scanner was used, the battery level, turn sound on/off, adjust interior light, and open the safe from the app is great. The safe does make a distinct opening sound that is audible to anyone within the same room and the lid opens 90 degrees automatically when opened. The keypad does light up when you use it, which is a nice feature.
I'm disappointed one of the biggest selling features of this safe, the Biometric scanner, didn't work as advertised and had such a high fail rate in my experience. I'll try one more VT20i and report my results.
text_fidelity_b: VAULTEK VS20i Biometric Handgun Bluetooth 2.0 Smart Safe Pistol Safe with Auto-Open Lid and Rechargeable Battery (Biometric)

Portable Pilates Bar Kit with Premium & Upgraded 30LB Thick Resistance Bands. Portable Gym Equipment For Home Exercise Bands. Multiple Use. Elastic Foot Loops Resistance Bands Workout Bar, Yoga Bar kit, & Exercise Bar. Exercise is important, as I am sure most would agree. But often, it isn’t practical to pay a visit to a nearby gym- you need something that is easily accessible and that you can take with you, wherever you go, for a quick workout. A good option for your workout needs is Portable Pilates Bar Kit with Premium & Upgraded 30LB Thick Resistance Bands.

Pulled from the package, this workout equipment is ready to use. All you need to do is attach the ends of the workout bar. At this point, you can use the foot loops to hold it down, then start exercising. There are several different ways you can use this simple piece of equipment. It can be used to tone different muscle groups depending on how it is used.

You do get a fairly good amount of resistance from this workout bar, but there is no way to control the level of resistance. You have to take it the way it is, since there is no way to adjust it, that I can see. It seems to work fine for basic needs. Once you have used it for a while, I would guess that will no longer be sufficient- it will get too easy and you will likely need something with greater resistance. In other words, this cannot take the place of the sophisticated workout equipment in a well- stocked gym. But the best part about it is that, since it is so small and compact, you can use it whenever you need it.

The best way to utilize the Portable Pilates Bar is to find different ways to do the exercises. I recommend going online and looking for different exercises so that you can workout different muscle groups. It’s a nice, simple piece of exercise equipment and it is useful for those who are on the go and need something to encourage exercise anytime, anyplace.
text_fidelity_b: Portable Pilates Bar Kit with Premium & Upgraded 30LB Thick Resistance Bands. Portable Gym Equipment For Home Exercise Bands. Multiple Use. Elastic Foot Loops Resistance Bands Workout Bar, Yoga Bar kit, & Exercise Bar.

text_fidelity_a:
Coghlans 0008 Camp Knife This is just the right size for my medium size hands and disappears in my pocket. Fit and finish are great. There are no flaws in the Opinel blade locking ring, or handle. When properly locked open there is no play in the blade in any direction. Opening and closing the unlocked blade require a little effort which is the way that I like it. The wood handle is varnished. The locking ring is stiff and requires quite a bit more than my 12 year old Opinel. This is reported to ease up after using it for a while and I don't find it to be objectionable. Shaving sharpness is there too. This knife totally meets my expectations and requirements.
The dimensions of this knife are:

4-1/4" closed
3-1/4" Blade
7-1/2 Total Length open

The best attributes of this knife are the curved handle and the carbon blade. The standard Opinel handle is one of only two ways to get an Opinel with a carbon steel blade. It has a straight body with a larger bump on the end. The handle of this Coghlan's version looks to be the same handle that comes in the Opinel Garden Knife #8. It is the curved design with the size and heft of the standard Opinel. This Coghlan's version is perfect size and model for me. This knife comes in three sizes, "7, #8, and #9. The #8 fits my hand perfectly.

The carbon blade requires special care. To avoid tarnishing and rusting keep a very thin coat of oil on the blade and avoid acid such as are found in fruits. If you want this knife in stainless steel with a drop point blade shape rather than the standard clip point check out the Opinel Garden Knife #8.
text_fidelity_b: Coghlans 0008 Camp Knife

text_fidelity_a:
MinnKota Riptide 55 ST Bowmount Trolling Motor with i-Pilot and No Foot Pedal (55lbs Thrust, 54" Shaft) I bought one of these for my 18' Carolina Skiff. I also bought the quick release mount. I bought the quick release mount so I could remove the trolling motor when travelling long distances with the boat. I fish from MD to the Gulf and bouncing down the road wouldn't be be good for it. First impression is that I'm going to like it a lot. I've been in the water twice using the trolling motor, both times in salt water, which is where I spend most of my fishing time. Installation was easy and deploying and retracting the ST55 is also easy. The iPilot anchor function worked well in 1.5 mph currents and 12 knot winds. I'll try it in the 8kt currents in the OBX in August. I like the iPilot control unit and no foot pedal because I'm not restricted to a certain place in the boat. I maxed it out and was surprised at how strong the motor was. I used the motor for about 2 hours and battery drain was about 1.4 volts from 14.2 to 12.8. Totally acceptable, especially for the size boat and winds. The instructions call for a 60 amp inline circuit breaker, however, I'm using a 40 amp and it was fine on full power. I've given it a 4 star rating right now and will return to add more to this review once I've used the programming features of the iPilot.

Update 24 Feb 15: I have nothing but praise for Min-Kota and the RipTide ST55. I've put about 70 hours on this motor and spent many hours in the anchor mode against 2-3 knot tides. I didn't use my boat anchor once during the summer and fall months because the RipTide's anchor function is spot on. I mainly fish in saltwater and I've used it from Florida, to North Carolina, to Maryland and its performance is outstanding. The only down side is it doesn't have automatic deploy and retrieve. I know Min-Kota is working on one. I love the iPilot! I can use it from anywhere on the boat and only have to remember when facing backwards, left is right and right is left. Duh. Most definitely 5 STARS
text_fidelity_b: MinnKota Riptide 55 ST Bowmount Trolling Motor with i-Pilot and No Foot Pedal (55lbs Thrust, 54" Shaft)

Ivation 5-Gallon Portable Outdoor Shower - Lightweight & Portable - Includes Removable Hose w/On-Off Switchable Showerhead I received this as a free review sample. I am not going to repeat the product specs on this page since the material and unfolded dimensions are provided by the manufacturer. I will give my take on this and reasons why I rated it so highly.

What I especially like is the compact size that it folds to. Out of the box it's only 12.5x4x1 inches, which will fit in a backpack or even in the glove box of most vehicles (especially if you fold it over lengthwise.)

There is a slight chemical odor as soon as you unbox it, so I recommend airing it out before refolding and storing it for actual use. It takes about an hour for the odor to dissipate.

Using it is as simple as placing your valuables inside, folding over the reinforced rib at the top (the mouth) of the bag two or three times, then doubling and using the closure snaps. You are NOT supposed to press the air out because that will provide buoyancy in the event that it falls into water. I am not sure how much weight it will take to achieve negative buoyancy, but partially filled with air it will support a good five pounds and still maintain a degree of positive buoyancy. The key point and why I rated this so highly is I tested it with a towel and a brick and it kept the towel completely dry.

If you camp, boat or spend time at the beach and want to safeguard wallets, phones and tablets, this bag will do the trick.
text_fidelity_b: Ivation 5-Gallon Portable Outdoor Shower - Lightweight & Portable - Includes Removable Hose w/On-Off Switchable Showerhead

text_fidelity_a:
30MP 4K WiFi Hunting Game Trail Camera with 120°Wide Angle Monitor, Less Than 0.2s Trigger Time,Night Vision Motion Activated Waterproof Cameras, Send Pictures and Videos to Cell Phone Via Bluetooth You can get good-quality trail cameras for a lot less than this one, albeit not 4K or with as many features, but I wanted to try this one with bluetooth/wifi capability and the ability to view remotely from your phone via an app. I was also hoping to be able to download the images from the camera to my phone without having to fiddle with the memory card.

I plan to use this camera with a solar panel to keep it charged up. What I discovered is that a charged solar panel hooked to this camera will power it on, but I couldn't get the setup menu to work properly. Thinking it was probably because the camera requires batteries even if the power is not coming from the batteries, I ordered 8 AA batteries and installed them today.

After another few hours of frustration, I've decided the wifi feature of this camera is just not going to work. I have followed the instructions to a T, but I've only been able to connect to the trail camera's wifi network once, and then I could not get the Android app to allow me to look at the camera's visuals or images. Other than the 4K definition, this camera really doesn't do much more than the one I already had that cost a LOT less. It did come with a 32GB memory card, which is really nice, but I'll still have to take the card out of the camera to dump its contents onto my computer, which is a pain. I didn't want to have to unmount and take down the camera at all but to dump its contents to my phone, wipe the memory card, and be done with it.

Speaking of the app, I'm not even sure the app I finally installed (WiFiTrailCamera) is what I need to work with this camera. The instructions do not include the name of the app but only state to scan a QCode; I only found what I think might be the required app by searching online for clues. Scanning the QCode offered me some kind of smart app that required setting up an account (which made me very nervous!) and also seemed to have something to do with enterprise teams. It had nothing whatsoever to do with a trail camera. I didn't know that until I reluctantly signed up for an account so I could set up the app and review the trail camera, and then I had to uninstall it and cancel my account. QCode fail!

So right now, I'm giving this a rather positive three stars because the wifi doesn't work and the app doesn't work. I have yet to actually see any images or videos it has taken, because I just got it installed outside after a week's worth of waiting for batteries and hours of trying to get it set up, but assuming they turn out to be as high quality as advertised, I'll leave this at three stars. If the image quality is as much of a disappointment as the wifi and app were, I'll come back and take off another star.

UPDATE: Complete fail. I cannot get the camera to come on in Test mode or in On mode. It was working when I left it on its mount last night, but this morning the camera is dead and apparently did not record anything during the night. I've checked all connections repeatedly and gone through the procedures countless times. What a ripoff! I'm going back to my cheapie trail camera, which I can count on to do the job.
text_fidelity_b: 30MP 4K WiFi Hunting Game Trail Camera with 120°Wide Angle Monitor, Less Than 0.2s Trigger Time,Night Vision Motion Activated Waterproof Cameras, Send Pictures and Videos to Cell Phone Via Bluetooth

text_fidelity_a:
MSR Hydromedary Hydration Bag Been using Dromedary and Dromedary Lite's for 20 years - totally came to trust them on many expeditions (PCT, JMT, 14er's, and winter alpine treks) - bought 2 of these and they both leak. MSR changed the caps or cap supplier and the new caps are defective. I screwed on one of the caps from a Dromedary Lite I purchased 15 years ago, and it would not leak. The old caps, which have been supplied as recently as a year ago, have "wash and dry after each use" molded on them. The new caps do not and are thicker on the edges and have sharper grip teeth. Fix the caps and I will change the rating. In the mean time, I will probably have to buy Nalgene caps or something to replace the junk MSR is selling.

The design is top-notch. The fact that the caps are interchangeable with Nalgene, fit water filters, and the nylon bags are tougher than plastic are all a testament to the fact these bags can be the best. They're the only bag I trust to fill with hot water and slip in my sleeping bag in the winter. They're awesome, 5-star products if they're made correctly.

I have a hydromedary kit I used on the bigger bags (6L) for at least 15 years. I replaced the hose before with regular vinyl tubing from the hardware store. The tubing on this hydromedary is smaller in diameter but still looks like standard vinyl tubing and could easily be replaced.
text_fidelity_b: MSR Hydromedary Hydration Bag

Yes, they're both round & heavy. However, a medicine ball is usually (as in the case of this Nordic Fitness model) much larger & will have a slight bounce to it.

The slam ball is usually small & very dense. And normally will not bounce much (unless it's over inflated).

So while both can be used for similar exercises, if you really want to round out your routines, it's best to have both.

This medicine ball from Nordic Fitness is very well made & comes with a basic exercise guide & welcome letter.

iBert Child Bicycle Safe-T-Seat My daughter and I love this seat. I bought it because I did not want to haul a heavy trailer.

It is installed on my beach cruiser and it fits perfectly - plenty of room for me to reach the handlebars and pedal without the bike seat in the way. I am 5'4" short. It was easy to install. I am surprised at how stable and natural it feels.

I bought it when she was 10 months old, but she was too small to use it. I started using it when she was just over 1 yr and she fit much better (she is average size).

So far we do short rides around the neighborhood in the evenings and weekends and I can take her 1.5 miles to daycare, and she loves it. She can also look up and see me and ring the bell. We can talk about the things we see on the ride, unlike if we had a trailer.

She has fallen asleep twice while riding. There is nowhere for her head to go, but to slump sideways. I have just supported her head with my hand for the few minutes it takes me to get home.

One very nice aspect to this seat is that it mounts on the bike stem, so when she grabs the handlebars, she can't get any torque to steer the bike.

Mine came with the padding for the seat.

Cons:
The shoulder straps are a little strange - they can slide off her shoulder, but this won't be a problem when she is bigger.

The bar that comes down over the child's lap has a cheap attachment mechanism. This ought to be fixed in the next models - it is not acceptable for a product this expensive.

In a light rain (like we encountered last weekend), water puddles in the bottom of the foot cups - I might drill a hole on the bottom of each one (we live in the Pacific NorthWest).
text_fidelity_b: iBert Child Bicycle Safe-T-Seat

So, I asked for my treadmill to be delivered to my condo unit. I asked for them to buzz the door so they can wheel it to my door.

Plus I used some of the comments that people made to Amazon on somethings the manual did not state or I didn't want to look through the manual.

text_fidelity_a:
Delta Cycle Airzound Bike Horn - Loud 115 DB Bike Horn for Adults - Rechargeable, No Batteries Needed - Adjustable Volume - Weatherproof Thermoplastic - Bicycle Horn for Road and Mountain Bikes This is essentially one of those compressed air horns you hear at sports events or a boat 'mayday' alert only this is rechargeable. It has a standard Schrader valve that can be pumped up to 80 psi (5.5 bars). I have the AirXwills Electric Bike Pump, another great product here on Amazon, that can refill the bottle in 10 seconds. It took a while to find a placement on the handlebars where I could press the trigger quickly. I ended up modifying my grip and mounted it on the grip.

The design flaw is that, to be useful in an emergency, the trigger must be mounted very close to the handlebar grip. But the very loud horn is forever married to the trigger meaning that the horn is just 18 inches from your ear causing significant discomfort. In one way this might be good because it will discourage using it in any situation other than in a true emergency. I would have liked the horn instead to be married to the air bottle which could then allow placement of the horn further away from the ear, like low on the seat down tube or low on the fork. There's a volume control but even at the lowest volume it is still very loud.

With this horn people complain about two things: 1) the bottle diameter is too narrow to fit securely in a standard bottle cage and 2) it's a pain to have to thread and secure the air hose down a bike frame tube to a frame-mounted bottle cage. The iUKUS Adjustable Bike Water Bottle Holder, another good product here on Amazon, solves both problems. It mounts to the handlebars so no worries about threading the air hose; just put the excess hose in the bottom of the cage before inserting the bottle. And it is adjustable down to the 2 inches that will accommodate the Airzound horn bottle securely. I can even mount the bottle sideways so it isn't so conspicuous and it's still completely secure.

These are my only other minor complaints: 1) the air bottle makes the entire setup a little bulky and 2) the quick release system for the mount/trigger assembly is a little flimsy and difficult to operate.

I think they are being modest when they state that volume is 115 db. Even at the lowest volume the horn can be heard in a nearby car with windows closed, air conditioning and the radio on. This horn turns heads. Great product, great value.
text_fidelity_b: Delta Cycle Airzound Bike Horn - Loud 115 DB Bike Horn for Adults - Rechargeable, No Batteries Needed - Adjustable Volume - Weatherproof Thermoplastic - Bicycle Horn for Road and Mountain Bikes

Perfect Life Ideas 3 Pack Camping Lanterns LED Lamps Emergency Lights for Home Vehicle Travel Emergencies - Garage Office Desk Camp Rv Boat. Battery Operated Lighting Gear. Cordless. Brand Tm These are small - roughly the same size as a coke can - and that makes them the perfect size for some very specific uses. They weigh almost nothing, even with the four AA batteries inserted. The little handle on top is just tall enough to hang these lanterns from a drawer pull or in our house, a push down style door knob. With the light weight, the lantern hangs without affecting the use of the door handle so you can have light in an interior room or basement while hunting for a fuse box etc and know where the exit is. I also like that the exterior of the lantern is a bit of a rubberized texture - setting it on our marble bathroom counter in the dark wasn't as risky as it would've been with just slick plastic. These are small and weigh very little - a slippery surface or wet hands could be a problem without the textured case.

The light is very bright and clear white. No yellow hue to it at all and these LED bulbs turn on instantly. We tested the lights in a pitch black garage, closet and walking around in the back yard at 11pm. They are bright enough to use to get dressed or find your way around the garage with no problems at all. Use in the yard was fine, but a flashlight is better as a directional aimed beam for walking. My one star deduction is because I dropped one of the lanterns from hip high and it came apart when it landed (a fall of two feet onto a thick bath mat). The batteries flew out and the bottom cracked apart. However - the light DID work afterwards and we just super glued the crack back together. I'll keep these in the bathroom, garage and kitchen for power outages in the future. I received a sample set for testing and review.

text_fidelity_a:
DEERFAMY Easy Pop Up Tent, 3 Person Pop Up Tent for Camping, Tent Instant Pop Up with Vestibule Army Green Pop Up Camping Tent for Family Ok, let's get something straight- there's no way 3-4 adults are fitting in this thing. But that's normal for tent ratings- they are usually a little bit generous with their occupancy rating and assume bodies are stacked like sardines inside. But this is more like half capacity at best- I'd say maybe 2 adults, or one adult and 2 kids. However, that did NOT stop 3 of my kids from wanting to run inside the very second it popped open. They fit comfortably inside and honestly it makes a great kid's tent if you want, for example, to have a separate adults' tent or even just let the kids have a backyard sleepover. We haven't used it in the rain yet so I can't vouch for that sort of use, but I CAN say that it pops open effortlessly by just removing it from the bag it comes in. Easiest tent install ever! Putting it back in? That's a challenge.
I like that it comes with directions sewn into the bag, but they were still hard to follow if you haven't done a tent fold like this before. It is similar to those car windshield pop up protectors in that it has plastic circular hoops that need to fold along itself to make a large oval into smaller circles. And if you make a mistake, it will POP open in your face and make you start over. That was annoying. But I did eventually get it to the correct size folding on the third try, and was able to get it back in the back and zip it up.
At $70, you can get a much bigger tent from Coleman or Ozark Trail, but not a pop up kind like this one. The instant pop ups fetch a premium, and I recall the last one I saw was slightly bigger than this one but nearly 2x the price, so I think it is priced appropriately for what it is. I'd consider this one a good value, I just wish it was easier to put away, and was a little more realistic about capacity.
text_fidelity_b: DEERFAMY Easy Pop Up Tent, 3 Person Pop Up Tent for Camping, Tent Instant Pop Up with Vestibule Army Green Pop Up Camping Tent for Family

text_fidelity_a:
Ibera Bicycle Bag PakRak Clip-On Quick-Release All Weather Bike Panniers (Pair), Includes Rain Cover , Black These are nice looking and well constructed panniers. However, they have a few issues that leave me not fully satisfied.

First, there is not a single hook, loop, strap, or D ring for you to attach anything to. No place to attach a reflector or a tail light, no place to attach bungees, nothing. Seriously? Has whoever designed these every ridden a bike? There's always something you want to attach somewhere. How hard is it to add a few strategically placed D rings and maybe a strap for a clip-on light?

Second, other than the very flat zippered pocket on the top flap, there is not a divider or a pocket anywhere, inside or out. Everything you put in this pannier is just bouncing around with everything else in there. I like to keep my tools, my spare inner tube, a rag, a few wipes and a few zip ties with me at all times. I'd like to keep all these supplies in a pocket separate from my groceries, laptop, .... But no. There's not a pocket anywhere for a road kit. I had to buy ditty bags and put my emergency kit in those, and toss those in the bottom of these bags, where they continue to bounce around with everything else. But at least they bounce around together.

Third, I find these bags unnecessarily difficult to close. There's a bit of elastic at the back of the cover, near the rack, that does not glide smoothly over the body of the bag. Every single time I close these bags, I have to grab the elastic on both sides and pull it into place for a snug fit. It does make the bag look nice and neat when closed, and maybe it helps keep rain out. But it's annoying that I can't just flip the flap over and close the bag. Also, the clips that hold the top flap down are surprisingly finicky. I'm not sure why, but I have to slide the tab into the clip exactly parallel or it won't go in.

Fourth, the bags do not collapse when empty.They ship flat, and I assumed that I could collapse them at least a little bit when they're empty. But no. They ship with rigid pieces of plastic that you slide into very snug slots to give them structure and shape. You do not want to remove these every time you empty the bag and reinsert them when you load the bag. And even if you did remove them, the bag would just flop around loosely - you can't cinch it so it's smaller. So these bags are always the same (generous) size no matter how much or how little you have in them.

Finally, the bag claims to fit most racks. IT DOES NOT. The clips on top probably do fit over a variety of sizes of rack tubes. And the tab that releases the top clips is a really nice touch, and works well. The problem is the bottom clip, the one that keeps the bag from flapping around when you turn. It is a fixed distance from the top clips, and the distance is very short! I saw that before I purchased these, but I thought I'd be able to rotate the clip so it could grab on to one of the tubes going down to the bottom of my rack. WRONG. That clip does not move up or down, and it does not rotate - you can only slide it left and right. So if the bottom tube of your rack isn't exactly 7" from the top tube, the bottom clip won't connect. I had to remove the bottom clip, flip it upside down, then use a 10" bungee to stretch between the bottom tube of my rack and the inverted clip on this bag. It's a reasonably snug fit and it works well enough. But, contrary to its claims, this bag did not fit my rack - I had to jerry-rig it.

I'm keeping the bags, because I do like the quick on-and-off feature. And they're good sized, and they look sharp. But with a few tweaks to the design they could've been perfect. They're not.
text_fidelity_b: Ibera Bicycle Bag PakRak Clip-On Quick-Release All Weather Bike Panniers (Pair), Includes Rain Cover , Black

text_fidelity_a:
WLOOD Golf Cart Speaker Mount, Universal Portable Adjustable Strap Fits Most Bluetooth Wireless Speakers Attachment Accessory Holder Bar Rail Who wouldn’t love some great tunes on their golf cart..?!! As a family who owns a golf cart yet, has never golfed a day in our life - we’ve spent the last decade doing nothing but, fun rides and adventures all around our planned community with our kiddos on this toy. Music would only enhance this- and give us golf cart karaoke?!!

Problem is.. this is a one size fits most. But, it didn’t come close to being “most” for us! How.. when we have the same speaker used in the sellers sample photo description- see photo I included..??!! Right from start when trying to attach we had issues.. this has 6 velcro straps coming out of the sides- (picture a big bug with legs!) Zero instructions included and you'd think this would be straightforward.. Trust me, we tried straps forward wrapping around pole and then, backwards just the same- we even went back to description online.. studied the photo and still had no success.

Problems we incurred:

•Straps are not long enough to wrap around the pole and speaker- and have enough length to close on themself. (this is placing the speaker in same spot as advertised!)

•2 of the 3 sets of straps were sewn in backwards- so, if wrapping around the direction they’re attached- The Velcro teeth on x2 straps are on the wrong side. (Equivalent to getting two negative signs together..) hoping this is an error!

•From photo description it appears we are missing a middle extra strap? Photo shows x1 in brown strap thru middle but, we don’t have anything of the sort...??

•This has no bottom support or “shelf” for added protection.. this could lead speaker slide at the bottom if it were to become a loose. Golf carts bounce around a bit and vibration may cause this to slip. So, bottom support would be helpful if not, necessary to protect the speaker from falling down and give the user peace of mind.

•This is missing a simple but straightforward set of instructions.

overall, this may work with a much smaller size speaker- one with hardly any girth.. Even then, it may be hit/miss to get the securely fastened. I’m afraid a smaller speaker may not produce enough sound to be heard over a motorized golf cart and will it stay safe? In leui of listing this “one size fits all/most..” this would be beneficial to list the actual length and dimension of straps so, one can verify speaker sizes that would work! Listed at a price point of $10- this could be a great find.. if, it could be successful. Tbh, It may be safer to invest more solid option to ensure it will fit/function as expected. I hope this info can help your decision… Feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: WLOOD Golf Cart Speaker Mount, Universal Portable Adjustable Strap Fits Most Bluetooth Wireless Speakers Attachment Accessory Holder Bar Rail
